A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RefVFX research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including the expanded user study in v4.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation comparisons, human preference results in Tables 1–2, similarity measurements in Tables 3–4, and supplementary video-quality measurements in Table 10.

after.justification: V4 retains original generation and quantitative results and reports a revised human study, including Overall Match judgments and bootstrap uncertainty.

M1.justification: The data-generation pipelines, reference-latent concatenation, conditioning masks, training procedure, and inference guidance remain unchanged. References to an 'updated conditioning' scheme describe the architecture already documented in v1, rather than a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LoRA-derived I2V, neural V2V, and programmatic V2V coverage. Section 4.1 retains 28 unseen LoRA effects, 56 reference videos, and the existing V2V scenarios. V4 clarifies their organization and use of real input videos without establishing newly added coverage.

E2.justification: V4 adds Lucy Edit to the code-based V2V human-preference and similarity comparisons in Tables 1 and 4, where v1 has dashes. The comparator sets in the other corresponding comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The primary human evaluation changes from five-level ratings to two-alternative forced choice and adds Overall Match alongside the existing adherence criteria. V1 reports 669, 455, and 252 annotations across its three tasks; v4 reports over 15,000 annotations from over 500 annotators. Training and automatic evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 1–2 extend the existing No Ref ablation to Overall Match, adding evidence about reference conditioning's contribution to jointly transferring effects and preserving input content. The guidance sensitivity example in Figure 8 and failure analysis in Figure 9 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: V1 reports win rates and mean preference scores without uncertainty estimates. V4 reports bootstrap standard deviations throughout Tables 1–2; Appendix C specifies 10,000 iterations resampling annotators and trials. This adds uncertainty estimation to the primary evaluation, without establishing additional model-training runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 replace the human-study results and add Overall Match scores. For example, I2V preference against Wan2.1 changes from 74.7% to 57.1 ± 2.4% under the revised procedure, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Table 4 adds Lucy Edit's code-based input/reference similarities of 0.8882/0.6539. Tables 3 and 10 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The triplet construction definitions, guidance equations (1)–(5), and supplementary motion-quality expression (6) are retained. No mathematical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about reference-based temporal effect transfer, the large training dataset, joint conditioning, unseen-effect generalization, and superiority over baselines. The introduction clarifies the framework's components without changing these claims.

C2.justification: V4 newly interprets its bootstrap deviations as confirming statistical reliability and discusses the near-chance input-adherence result against No Ref. This reliability interpretation is stronger than near-chance entries warrant. The under-editing explanation and Appendix A limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents MTurk recruitment, randomized presentation, 30 distinct annotators per experiment, five practice trials, and the study interface. V4 also specifies Wan2.1 in the main implementation description and changes the project-page link target. Existing training, inference, hardware, and runtime details are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion remain unchanged. The positioning against text-driven editing, static reference conditioning, and effect-specific finetuning is retained; reference back-reference changes reflect pagination.

P1.justification: V4 makes localized revisions to the introduction, method overview, dataset terminology, validation description, and user-study discussion. It inserts a user-study appendix, renumbers the subsequent appendix sections, and adds acknowledgments while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain Overall Match columns and revised captions, and Figure 10 newly illustrates the study interface. V4 also changes a Figure 3 transition label, identifies Table 5 as a subset, and relocates Table 4. Existing qualitative and architecture illustrations are retained.

improvement.justification: V4 substantially strengthens the paper's primary empirical validation. It replaces a sparsely documented preference study without uncertainty reporting with a larger, explicitly specified study, adds joint assessment of effect transfer and content preservation, and reports annotator/trial bootstrap uncertainty (Section 4.3 and Appendix C). These changes address important weaknesses in assessing and reproducing the central evidence. The blanket reliability claim remains overstated for near-chance results such as 51.3 ± 3.1%, but the evaluation is materially more transparent and informative.
